label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, provider-outage, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 10 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Its diagnosis named no action, so nobody was asked to approve one. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing: this fault's cause is not a deploy.

case.name: provider-outage
case.title: Payments fail: the provider hangs, and our circuit breaker fails fast
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: the provider's charge and refund API hangs (5 s, then 503): our payments API's calls to it time out, each after 3 attempts, until its circuit breaker opens, after 5 calls in a row got no answer; from then on it fails fast, answering 503 'outcome unknown' at once without calling the provider, and lets one trial call through 10 s after it opened, and again after each trial that fails.
case.remedy: nothing to change on our side: the provider must recover (escalate to it). Meanwhile the circuit breaker keeps the API answering at once, and closes again when a trial call gets an answer. After it recovers, the payments and refunds left pending need a decision (retry them with their keys, or mark them failed): a refund left pending blocks new refunds on its payment until it settles

expected_symptoms: clients get 503 'outcome unknown', most of them at once: the 5xx share of POST /payments climbs

the first calls still wait out their 3 timed-out attempts (about 10 s) until the breaker opens; after that only the trial calls wait, the first 10 s after it opened, then one 10 s after each that fails: the p95 latency may climb for about a minute, then drops
provider calls end with no answer (timeouts) at first, klaxon.provider.attempts result no_answer; then the breaker refuses them, klaxon.provider.refused
the payments API logs 'circuit breaker open', and its health check keeps passing: once the breaker opens, its worker threads are free again
the money check passes: nothing was charged, so no money is wrong

after it ends, the next trial call gets an answer and the breaker closes; payments and refunds whose outcome stayed unknown stay pending, with nothing charged or refunded: they need a decision (retry them with their keys, or mark them failed), and until then such a refund blocks new refunds on its payment

alert.name: PaymentsErrorsHigh
alert.summary: Payments are failing: over the last minute, 95% of the answers to POST /payments on payments-api were 5xx (8.87 per second), above the threshold of 20%. Payments are slow: over the last minute, the p95 latency of POST /payments on payments-api was 4.2 s, above the threshold of 2 s.

diagnosis.hypothesis: The payment provider (fake-provider, external) began failing around 10:49 to 10:51. Its 500s rose while its 200s fell to zero by 10:51:20 (c4), and some calls hung until our 3 s read timeout. In the slow trace, one POST /payments made two provider attempts, each a 3 s ReadTimeout, 6.2 s in all (c7). Other slow requests sit near 3 s and 6 s (c6), and these timeouts explain the 4.2 s p95. The failures opened payments-api's circuit breaker (PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, c3), so it now fails fast with 503 'payment left pending' (c2, c1). Not a deploy regression: every container was created together at 10:48:52 with normal settings (c3). Money check passed (c8). Open: the client p95 of about 9 ms (c5) counts only completed calls, and the provider's own cause is outside our view.

evidence.shows: POST /payments 503s jumped to about 10.25/s at 10:51:11, while 201s fell to about 0.4/s.
payments-api errors: '/v1/payments not sent: the circuit breaker is open', with each payment left pending.
All services were created at once at 10:48:52 with nominal settings, so no single change explains this. PROVIDER_BREAKER=on.
Provider 500s rose from 0.09/s to 0.24/s while its 200s fell from 3.2/s to 0 by 10:51:20.
Slow POST /payments and refund traces of about 3 s and 6.2 s, multiples of the 3 s timeout.
One payment made two provider calls, each a 3 s httpx ReadTimeout, then answered 503 after 6.2 s.
Money check passed every invariant: ledger balanced and matching the provider, no double charges, 237 payments never charged.

proposed_fix.summary: No rollback on our side: the breaker is working and keeping money safe. Escalate to the provider about its 500s and timeouts. Watch for the breaker's trial calls to succeed so it closes. Once the provider recovers, make sure pending payments are retried or reconciled through their idempotency keys, then run money_check again.

diagnosis.blast_radius: This changes nothing in the system. Until the provider recovers, payments stay pending or answer 503, so clients see failures meanwhile.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Nothing to undo, since no change is made. If breaker or timeout settings are changed later, revert them with rollback_deploy of payments-api.
